summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the Planted series with a message titled Planted in God's Church, the third part of a series that began with being planted in God's Word and being planted with God's people. After opening in prayer and inviting everyone to connect with those around them, Pastor Travis shared his testimony. He described how, after a very low moment as a teenager, God met him and brought him into a church community. Serving there discipled him, moved him away from unhelpful influences, and gave him new godly friends. He also shared that his wife's life was transformed through the same kind of church community after a difficult season. His conviction is that Jesus saves and changes us, and that being planted in the church is a vital part of continued growth.

Anchoring the message in Psalm 92:12-14, he taught that the righteous flourish when they are planted in the house of the Lord. Believing in God is not the same as being rooted, and he encouraged the church to be doers of the word, not only hearers. His first point was that the church is not a place we attend but a house we are planted in. The church is also a body, as 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12 describe, so connection through relationships, community, and accountability matters, and every part of the body is significant. His second point was that planted people serve and do not just sit. Drawing on Hebrews 10:24-25, 1 Peter 4:10, and the example of Jesus, who came to serve, he said church is not about what we get but about what we give. He used the image of a river versus a reservoir, saying we were rescued to be a river, and he named practical needs on the serve team, such as prayer team members, greeters, ushers, and drivers. His third point was that planted people build the house. He urged believers to move from spectator to stakeholder, to take ownership instead of offense, to stay through discomfort and forgive, and to help make the church better rather than critique it from a distance. He reminded the congregation that the church is the bride of Christ and that Jesus promised to build his church.

Pastor Travis closed by inviting anyone who wanted to give their life to Jesus for the first time to pray, and by inviting those ready to move from the bench to serving to respond. He then prayed for them to have follow-through and commitment to take their next step. He announced the Get in the Game membership class that evening at 5:00 p.m. as a way to learn the vision of Impact Church and step into serving. The online team encouraged viewers to download the Impact Church app, fill out the connection card, scan the QR code to share a decision to follow Jesus, and consider giving, trusting that what God is planting will grow into something strong and lasting.
mainPoints: The church is not a place we attend but a house we are planted in, and a body we are connected to through relationships, community, and accountability.
Planted people serve and do not just sit, because church is not about what we get but about what we give, using our gifts to serve others.
Planted people build the house, moving from spectator to stakeholder by taking ownership instead of offense and helping make the church better.

versesMentioned.text: Do not be misled: "Bad company corrupts good character."

The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, they will grow like a cedar of Lebanon; planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God. They will still bear fruit in old age, they will stay fresh and green,
The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
You believe that there is one God. Good! Even the demons believe that, and shudder.
Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.
Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.
For just as each of us has one body with many members, and these members do not all have the same function, so in Christ we, though many, form one body, and each member belongs to all the others.

And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

Jesus replied: 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.' This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.
Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms.

Monday.scripture: Psalm 92:13 (NIV): "planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God."
Monday.focus: Moving from attending church to being planted in it.
Monday.action: Write down three ways you are connected to Impact Church right now (for example a group, a serve team, or a friendship). Circle one area where you want to be more rooted and take one small step toward it today, such as downloading the app or filling out the connection card.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank you for your church. Help me to be more than an attender. Plant me deeply in your house so that I can grow and bear fruit for you. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: 1 Corinthians 12:12 (NIV): "Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ."
Tuesday.focus: Belonging to the body of Christ through real relationships.
Tuesday.action: Send a text or make a call to someone from church you do not know well. Ask how they are doing and how you can pray for them. If you are new, introduce yourself to someone at your next gathering.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, thank you for making me part of one body. Help me to connect with others, to be known, and to know others, so that no one feels alone. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Hebrews 10:24 (NIV): "And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds,"
Wednesday.focus: Encouraging others and being a builder instead of a critic.
Wednesday.action: Write a short note or message of encouragement to a pastor, volunteer, or church friend. Thank them for something specific they have done.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, make me an encourager. Keep me from a critical spirit, and show me how I can help build up your church. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 1 Peter 4:10 (NIV): "Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms."
Thursday.focus: Discovering and using your gifts to serve.
Thursday.action: List three skills or strengths God has given you. Look at the serve teams at Impact Church (such as greeters, ushers, prayer team, or drivers) and choose one to explore. Sign up or ask a leader how to get started.
Thursday.prayer: God, thank you for the gifts you have placed in me. Show me where to use them for others, and give me the courage to say yes. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Mark 10:45 (NIV): "For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
Friday.focus: Following the heart of Jesus by serving others.
Friday.action: Do one practical act of service for someone today without being asked, such as helping a neighbor, bringing a meal, or offering a ride. Do it quietly and without expecting anything in return.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for serving me and giving your life for me. Give me a servant's heart so that I give and not only receive. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: James 1:22 (NIV): "Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says."
Saturday.focus: Becoming a doer of the word and preparing to be planted this Sunday.
Saturday.action: Plan ahead for church tomorrow. Decide what time you will arrive, invite someone to come with you, and think about one way you can serve or help while you are there. Take a few minutes to pray for your pastors and church family.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, help me to do what your word says. Prepare my heart for worship tomorrow, and use me to bless others in your house. Amen.

title: Why You’re Not Growing Spiritually (And How to Fix It) | Planted in God’s Church
